theory.intro: **Fuel consumption** is how much fuel a vehicle uses for the distance it travels. It is written either as $\text{km/L}$ or as $\text{L/100 km}$. A higher $\text{km/L}$ is more efficient, but a lower $\text{L/100 km}$ is more efficient.
facts: $\text{km/L}$ is distance divided by fuel, so a car going $500$ km on $50$ L does $10$ km/L.
$\text{L/100 km}$ is the fuel used per $100$ km, found from $\dfrac{\text{litres}}{\text{km}} = \dfrac{x}{100\text{ km}}$.
To swap between the two rates use $\text{L/100 km} = \dfrac{100}{\text{km/L}}$, and also $\text{km/L} = \dfrac{100}{\text{L/100 km}}$.
The two rates run in opposite directions and are not directly proportional, so doubling $\text{km/L}$ halves $\text{L/100 km}$.
Fuel cost is the litres used multiplied by the price per litre, so always find the litres first.
steps: Write the given information as an equation using equivalent rates, letting the unknown be $x$
Solve for the unknown, taking the reciprocal of both sides first if $x$ is in the denominator
Multiply the litres by the price per litre when a cost is asked for

foundation.question_text: A hatchback used $40$ L of petrol to travel $620$ km. Calculate its fuel consumption rate in km/L.
A delivery van used $45$ L of diesel on a trip of $360$ km. Calculate its fuel consumption rate in L/100 km.
foundation.solution_text:
$\dfrac{45\text{ L}}{360\text{ km}} = \dfrac{x\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}$
$x = \dfrac{45}{360} \times 100$
$= 12.5\text{ L/100 km}$

foundation.question_text: A sedan has a fuel consumption rate of $12.5$ km/L. Express this rate in L/100 km.
A ute has a fuel consumption rate of $16$ L/100 km. Express this rate in km/L.
A hybrid car uses fuel at $7.5$ L/100 km. How much fuel does it use on a trip of $240$ km?
A station wagon uses fuel at $9.2$ L/100 km. How much fuel does it use on a trip of $350$ km?
A courier car uses fuel at $8.5$ L/100 km. How far can it travel on $34$ L of petrol?
foundation.solution_text:
$\dfrac{8.5\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}} = \dfrac{34\text{ L}}{x\text{ km}}$
$\dfrac{100\text{ km}}{8.5\text{ L}} = \dfrac{x\text{ km}}{34\text{ L}}$
$x = \dfrac{100}{8.5} \times 34$
$= 400\text{ km}$

foundation.question_text: A minibus uses fuel at $11$ L/100 km and its tank holds $55$ L. How far can it travel on a full tank?
foundation.solution_text:
$\dfrac{11\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}} = \dfrac{55\text{ L}}{x\text{ km}}$
$\dfrac{100\text{ km}}{11\text{ L}} = \dfrac{x\text{ km}}{55\text{ L}}$
$x = \dfrac{100}{11} \times 55$
$= 500\text{ km}$

development.question_text: Priya's car uses fuel at $6.5$ L/100 km. Petrol costs $\$1.80$ per litre. What is the fuel cost of a $420$ km trip?
A tour bus uses fuel at $9.4$ L/100 km and travels $1250$ km. Diesel costs $152.6$ cents per litre. Calculate the fuel cost, correct to the nearest cent.
Car P travels $14$ km/L. Car Q uses fuel at $7.5$ L/100 km. Comparing litres used per $100$ km, which car is more efficient?
development.solution_text:
Car P: $\dfrac{100}{14}$
$= 7.14\text{ L/100 km}$ (to $2$ d.p.)
Car Q: $7.5\text{ L/100 km}$
$7.14 < 7.5$, so Car P uses less fuel per $100$ km and is the more efficient car.

development.question_text: Car R uses fuel at $6.4$ L/100 km and Car S uses fuel at $6.9$ L/100 km. Over $900$ km, how much less fuel does Car R use?
Marco's car uses fuel at $5.8$ L/100 km on country roads and $8.4$ L/100 km in the city. He drives $260$ km in the country and $40$ km in the city. How much fuel does he use altogether?
Sione drives $28$ km to work and $28$ km home again on each of $5$ days, using $21$ L of petrol in total. Calculate his car's fuel consumption rate in L/100 km.
development.solution_text:
$\text{distance} = 28 \times 2 \times 5$
$= 280\text{ km}$
$\dfrac{21\text{ L}}{280\text{ km}} = \dfrac{x\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}$
$x = \dfrac{21}{280} \times 100$
$= 7.5\text{ L/100 km}$

development.question_text: A motorcycle travels $22$ km on each litre of fuel and its tank holds $14$ L. How far can it travel on a full tank?
A scooter travels $15$ km on each litre of fuel. How much fuel does it use on a trip of $600$ km?
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{15\text{ km}}{1\text{ L}} = \dfrac{600\text{ km}}{x\text{ L}}$
$\dfrac{1\text{ L}}{15\text{ km}} = \dfrac{x\text{ L}}{600\text{ km}}$
$x = \dfrac{600}{15}$
$= 40\text{ L}$

mastery.question_text: Nadia's workplace is $24$ km from home. Her car uses fuel at $8.5$ L/100 km and petrol costs $\$1.94$ per litre. A train pass covering $10$ one-way trips costs $\$38$. For $10$ one-way trips, which is cheaper and by how much?
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{distance} = 24 \times 10$
$= 240\text{ km}$
$\text{fuel} = 8.5 \times \dfrac{240}{100}$
$= 20.4\text{ L}$
$\text{cost} = 20.4 \times \$1.94$
$= \$39.576$
$\approx \$39.58$
$\$39.58 - \$38$
$= \$1.58$
The train is cheaper, by $\$1.58$ for the $10$ trips.

mastery.question_text: Heather's car uses fuel at $6.8$ L/100 km for highway driving and $9.6$ L/100 km for city driving. She makes a journey of $480$ km that includes $55$ km of city driving. How much fuel does the journey use?
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{highway} = 480 - 55$
$= 425\text{ km}$
Highway fuel: $6.8 \times \dfrac{425}{100}$
$= 28.9\text{ L}$
City fuel: $9.6 \times \dfrac{55}{100}$
$= 5.28\text{ L}$
$28.9 + 5.28$
$= 34.18\text{ L}$

mastery.question_text: One car is advertised as travelling $18$ km/L. A rival model is advertised at $5.2$ L/100 km. Comparing litres used per $100$ km, which is more efficient and by how much? Answer correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
First car: $\dfrac{100}{18}$
$= 5.56\text{ L/100 km}$ (to $2$ d.p.)
Rival: $5.2\text{ L/100 km}$
$5.56 - 5.2$
$= 0.36\text{ L/100 km}$
The rival model is the more efficient, using $0.36$ L less per $100$ km.
